instructions: The day before, or at least 3 hours ahead: put the lamb neck in a large pot with 6 cups of water and 1 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then skim off the foam that rises. Turn the heat to low, partly cover the pot, and simmer for about 1 1/2 hours, until the meat falls off the bone.
Transfer the lamb to a plate and let it cool for 10 minutes. Pull the meat off the bones, discard the bones and any fat, and shred the meat into small pieces.

Strain the broth into a clean pot. That should be about 5 cups. If it's short, add hot water to make 5 cups. If you're making this ahead, stop here. Chill the meat and the broth separately for up to 2 days.
In a bowl, whisk the yogurt, cornstarch, egg yolk, the juice of half the lemon and 1 cup of cold water until smooth. Keep the egg white for another use.
Heat the broth over medium heat until it's steaming but not boiling. Ladle about 1 cup of the hot broth into the yogurt mixture, whisking the whole time.

Pour the yogurt mixture slowly into the pot, stirring in one direction. Keep the heat at medium-low and keep stirring until the soup thickens slightly, 3 to 4 minutes. Don't let it boil hard or it can split.
Add the shredded lamb and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer gently for 2 minutes. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Take the pot off the heat.
In a small pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Stir in the paprika and cook for 20 seconds, until it smells toasty. Take the pan off the heat.
Ladle the soup into bowls and spoon the paprika butter over the top. Put the Aleppo pepper on the table for anyone who wants heat.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat, stirring, and don't let the soup boil.
advance_prep_notes: cook the lamb and broth up to 2 days ahead
method_notes: Nefis Yemek Tarifleri (4.86 from 78) leads: lamb neck broth finished with a yogurt, flour and egg yolk terbiye and butter with pepper flakes. Sofra and Milk Street use the same flour, yogurt, egg and lemon finish; the English wedding soup pages (Food.com, That's Nerdalicious) skip the yogurt, so they were not followed. Flour is swapped for cornstarch so the soup stays gluten-free, and the lead's pressure cooker is replaced with a stovetop simmer, which makes it a make-ahead soup rather than a 30 minute lunch. The pepper flakes go on the table to keep the base mild.
